newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Transalta NZ cashes up bonds.
newsitem.headline: Transalta NZ cashes up bonds.

text.p: TransAlta Energy has recouped more than half the money it paid for Wellington power supplier Capital Power by cashing up the bonds it received through the merger of EnergyDirect and Capital Power.
The merged company, TransAlta NZ, issued 221 million shares and $110 million each of capital notes and seven and 10-year bonds to bring the two businesses together.

Owning Capital Power outright and a 41 percent stake in EnergyDirect, TransAlta Energy was eligible for 63 percent of those instruments and has sold its bonds at face value of $139 million through an offer by underwriters First NZ Capital

TransAlta Energy spokesman Cameron Barton said the company sold its bonds because it was more interested in equity investments, rather than debt. It has retained its shares and capital notes and may use proceeds from the sale for further equity investments.
" don't think it's any secret that we're very interested in New Zealand," he told NZPA.

Buying Capital Power cost TransAlta Energy $243 million. It paid Wellington City Council $120 million for a 49 percent shareholding in 1994, but got back $32 million as its share of a $65 million loan which the company raised at the same time.
In June TransAlta paid a further $90 million for the council's remaining stake in Capital Power but also fronted up with $65 million to refinance the company's loan.
TransAlta NZ shares closed 9 cents higher at $1.75 on Wednesday.
